Histone modification reprogramming drives core pathological processes in diabetic nephropathy

Histone modification reprogramming drives core pathological processes in diabetic nephropathy. (A) Inflammatory axis. Persistent hyperglycemia (high glucose) and related metabolic stress reshape chromatin states in renal resident cells (tubular epithelial cells, mesangial cells) and infiltrating immune cells by dysregulating histone-modifying enzymes. Increased HAT activity elevates activating histone acetylation at inflammatory loci; for example, PCAF promotes transcription of adhesion molecules and chemokines by increasing local activating acetylation and promoter occupancy. In parallel, HDAC6 upregulation promotes inflammatory injury and pyroptosis, in part via NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Histone methylation reprogramming further amplifies inflammation: SET7/9 deposits activating H3K4me1/me2 to facilitate NF-κB pathway activation and inflammatory gene expression, while KDM6A removes repressive H3K27me3 at pro-inflammatory gene promoters, derepressing transcription and sustaining inflammation. (B) Fibrotic axis. High glucose cooperates with the TGF-β1/Smad signaling pathway to recruit chromatin modifiers and drive a pro-fibrotic transcriptional program. p300/CBP-mediated histone acetylation increases chromatin accessibility at profibrotic genes (e.g., PAI-1, p21), promoting assembly of transcriptional complexes and extracellular matrix (ECM) accumulation. Beyond canonical PTMs, metabolic reprogramming–driven lactate accumulation induces histone lactylation, which activates downstream transcriptional regulators (e.g., KLF5) and represses epithelial markers, thereby accelerating epithelial–mesenchymal transition and fibrosis progression. C Podocyte injury and multicellular epigenetic crosstalk. In podocytes, diabetic cues establish persistent epigenetic memory that alters expression of key functional genes and injury pathways. Dysregulated HDACs and methylation programs (e.g., EZH2-H3K27me3; H3K4me3-associated regulation involving DACH1/PTIP) shift the balance from protective to injurious transcriptional states, contributing to cytoskeletal dysfunction, podocyte loss, and proteinuria. Histone modifications also mediate pathogenic podocyte-endothelial communication: high glucose–stimulated podocytes release CCL2 to activate CCR2 on glomerular endothelial cells, triggering p38 MAPK/MSK1/2-dependent H3S10 phosphorylation (H3S10ph) and VCAM-1 upregulation, thereby amplifying endothelial dysfunction and disrupting the glomerular filtration barrier. PCAF p300/CBP-associated factor, ICAM-1 intercellular adhesion molecule 1, VCAM-1 vascular cell adhesion molecule 1, MCP-1 monocyte chemoattractant protein-1, HDAC histone deacetylase, NLRP3 NOD-, LRR- and pyrin domain-containing protein 3, KDM6A lysine demethylase 6 A, CitH3 citrullinated histone H3, NETs neutrophil extracellular traps, TGF-β transforming growth factor-beta, CBP CREB-binding protein, Smad2/3 Mothers against decapentaplegic homolog 2/3, PAI-1 plasminogen activator inhibitor-1, EZH2 enhancer of zeste homolog 2, Deptor DEP domain-containing mTOR-interacting protein, mTOR mechanistic target of rapamycin, ASH2L ASH2 like histone lysine methyltransferase complex subunit, HIPK2 homeodomain-interacting protein kinase 2, ADAM12 A disintegrin and metalloproteinase 12, Notch1 Neurogenic locus notch homolog protein 1, SUV39H1 suppressor of variegation 3–9 homolog 1, KLF5 Krüppel-like factor 5, ECM extracellular matrix, STAT1 signal transducer and activator of transcription 1, CaN calcineurin, SFRO-1 secreted frizzled-related protein 1, CCL2 C-C motif chemokine ligand 2, CCR2 C-C motif chemokine receptor 2, MAPK mitogen-activated protein kinase, MSK1/2 mitogen- and stress-activated kinase 1/2, SENP6 sentrin/SUMO-specific protease 6, EDN1 Endothelin-1
